rule.title: Flashloan/swap callback lacks msg.sender validation — direct invocation drains approved tokens

intent.attack_thesis: A flashloan or DEX swap callback function (executeOperation, uniswapV2Call, etc.) is externally callable without verifying that msg.sender is the legitimate lending pool or DEX pair. An attacker calls the callback directly with crafted parameters, causing the contract to transfer or approve tokens on behalf of users who delegated allowances.

reporting.title_template: Unprotected flashloan callback enables direct token drain
reporting.summary: Matches contracts exposing a flashloan/swap callback selector (executeOperation, uniswapV2Call, flashCallback, etc.) that makes external calls (token transfers/approvals) without validating msg.sender against the legitimate pool or router address.
reporting.user_summary: This contract has a flashloan callback function that anyone can call directly. The function transfers or approves tokens without checking that the caller is the legitimate lending pool. An attacker can invoke the callback with crafted parameters to drain tokens that users have approved to this contract.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies contracts with known DeFi callback selectors (Aave executeOperation, Uniswap V2/V3 flash callbacks, ERC-3156 onFlashLoan, Balancer receiveFlashLoan) that lack msg.sender validation. When the callback contains CALL opcodes (token transfers) without a branch condition comparing msg.sender to a stored pool address, an attacker can bypass the flash loan mechanism entirely and invoke the callback directly to execute arbitrary token operations using the contract's existing approvals.
reporting.exploit_narrative: The attacker identifies that users have approved tokens to the vulnerable contract (e.g., via a legitimate DeFi operation). The attacker then calls the flashloan callback function directly (without going through the lending pool), passing crafted parameters that cause the contract to transfer the approved tokens to the attacker. Since the callback never checks that msg.sender is the pool, the call succeeds.
exploit_preconditions: contract exposes a flashloan/swap callback selector
callback does not validate msg.sender == lending_pool/router
callback performs token transfers or approvals based on callback parameters
victims have approved tokens to the vulnerable contract
remediation_hints: validate msg.sender == LENDING_POOL at the start of every callback
store the pool address immutably (constructor or constant)
use OpenZeppelin's FlashLoanSimpleReceiverBase which enforces this check
never trust callback parameters for token routing without sender validation

preconditions: flashloan callback selector is externally reachable

steps.action: call the flashloan callback directly with crafted asset/amount/params; callback executes token transfer using existing approvals
steps.expected_state: approved tokens transferred to attacker without going through the lending pool

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker receives tokens that were approved to the vulnerable contract by other users
environment_requirements: existing token approvals to the vulnerable contract
